sections.h2: Who values and who collects property tax in Graves County, KY?
sections.html:
Graves County splits the job between the PVA and the sheriff. The Property Valuation Administrator appraises every parcel in the county, but the county's own PVA page states that the office neither sets tax rates nor collects tax. Collection belongs to the Graves County Sheriff's Office, and delinquent real estate bills move to the County Clerk.

The PVA office is at 1102 Paris Road, Suite 2, in Mayfield, phone (270) 247-3301, with listed hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Clerk's office is at the same street address, Suite 5, and its delinquent real estate tax line is (270) 247-1697. The sheriff serves the public from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central Time, Monday through Friday, and takes payment by mail, in person or on its website, using check, cash or card.

Assessment records are searchable online. The sheriff's tax page points owners to the qPublic site for Graves County parcel data.

sections.h2: When do Graves County tax bills go out, and what if one never arrives?
sections.html:
Graves County property taxes are payable to the sheriff starting October 1 of the assessment year. A bill that has not shown up by October 10 should be replaced: the sheriff recommends asking for a duplicate, which can be picked up at the office or printed from its website.

Mailing addresses come from the PVA, and the sheriff cannot change them. Address changes made after June of the tax year miss that year's printing, which is a common reason a seller's bill lands at an old address after a move.

The statewide schedule in KRS 134.015 sits behind the local one. Paying everything by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, November 2 through December 31 is face value, January adds 5 percent, and anything later carries 10 percent. Because tax is a personal debt of whoever owned the parcel on January 1, a mid-year buyer should settle the split with the seller in writing.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Graves County assessment?
sections.html:
You can only appeal after talking with the PVA's staff. The state's process runs on a fixed calendar tied to the first Monday in May, when the tax roll opens for 13 days of public inspection.

  • Request a conference with the PVA or a deputy during or before the inspection window and ask how the value was built.
  • File with the County Clerk by close of business on the workday after inspection ends.
  • Prepare proof: comparable sales, listings, insurance papers, construction costs and photos of physical problems.
  • Appear before the local board of assessment appeals, which sits 25 to 35 days after inspection closes and writes out its reasons for any change.

Owners may record the hearing on audio. Skipping the hearing after filing cuts off a later appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption save a Graves County owner?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Using the Census median owner-occupied value of $147,800, a Graves County home would be taxed on $98,700 after the deduction.

The county's PVA page notes that no exemption applies automatically. A formal application has to be filed with the PVA before any exemption is granted. Disabled applicants must have been receiving disability payments for the whole assessment period, and most must renew each year.

The exemption belongs to the owner who lives in the home, so it does not transfer to a buyer. A new owner who qualifies applies again at the PVA.

sections.h2: What happens to a Graves County tax bill after April 15?
sections.html:
Every bill still unpaid when business closes on April 15 leaves the sheriff and goes to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a lien recorded on the parcel. The sheriff's office states that it cannot collect prior-year taxes after that date.

Delinquent bill timeline under a regular collection schedule (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
StepTiming
First county attorney noticeWithin 30 days of transfer
Second notice with the sale dateAt least 20 days after the first, within 60 days of transfer
Newspaper advertisement30 to 45 days before the sale
Tax sale90 to 135 days after transfer

From the moment of transfer, interest runs at 1 percent per month, and the Clerk and county attorney add commissions. The Department of Revenue's example turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 at transfer and about $1,388 if paid within five business days. A third-party buyer who takes the certificate at the sale can add its own fees.

sections.h2: How should I handle taxes at a Graves County closing?
sections.html:
Settle the current year's bill in the contract, because the sheriff bills the January 1 owner and has no say in how a sale splits the year. Ask the sheriff or the Clerk for a payoff before the closing date so the title company can wire the exact figure.

  • Ask the Clerk at (270) 247-1697 whether any earlier year sits in delinquency, since a lien there survives the sale.
  • List the buyer's in-care-of mailing address in the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires, so the next bill is not sent to the seller.
  • Check the parcel on the qPublic search page to confirm the owner name and acreage match the deed.

Kentucky also charges a transfer tax of fifty cents per $500 of value, collected by the Clerk when the deed is recorded. Budget for that line along with the open tax bill.

sections.h2: How did the 2021 tornado affect Mayfield and Graves County?
sections.html:
A long-track tornado crossed Graves County on December 10, 2021, causing widespread damage in Mayfield. The Graves County Courthouse took major damage, according to the county's Wikipedia entry. Owners rebuilding or clearing a lot should ask the PVA how destroyed or rebuilt structures are valued as of the January 1 assessment date.

A cash buyer who accepts a property as it stands can close without repairs, and the deed is still recorded at the Clerk's office on Paris Road.

sections.h2: What is the Graves County housing market like?
sections.html:
Graves County is on the southwest edge of Kentucky in the Jackson Purchase and covers 552 square miles of land. Mayfield is the county seat and largest city, Wingo is the other incorporated city, and the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge reaches into the county. The county was formed in 1824, and dark-fired tobacco and a woolen mill with clothing makers shaped its early economy.

  • Population: 37,050 in 2025, up 1.1 percent since 2020.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 76.1 percent, with 14,139 households.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $147,800.
  • Median gross rent: $775, and 83 building permits in 2025.
  • Median household income: $50,772, with 16.6 percent of people in poverty.

With 83 permits issued in a county of more than 14,000 households, most Graves County sales are resale houses, so condition and clear title matter to buyers.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Graves County property taxes?
faqs.a: At the Graves County Sheriff's Office, by mail, in person or on its website. The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central Time, Monday through Friday, and accepts check, cash or card.

faqs.q: What if my Graves County tax bill did not arrive?
faqs.a: Ask the sheriff for a duplicate if it has not come by October 10. The mailing address on a bill comes from the PVA, so address changes made after June miss that year's bills.

faqs.q: Is the homestead exemption automatic in Graves County?
faqs.a: No. A formal application has to be filed with the Graves County PVA, at (270) 247-3301, before the $49,100 deduction is granted. You must be 65 or older or totally disabled.

faqs.q: When does a Graves County bill go to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: After the close of business on April 15. The bill becomes a certificate of delinquency, a lien is recorded, and 1 percent monthly interest begins along with clerk and attorney commissions.

faqs.q: Does a Graves County sale have to wait for delinquent taxes to be paid first?
faqs.a: No, but the lien follows the parcel, so the balance has to be paid at or before closing. The Clerk's delinquent tax line at (270) 247-1697 can give a current payoff figure.
